title: Trinity Sunday
hook: the Sunday after Pentecost is about who God is

segments.voice: Yesterday, Pentecost and the golden sequence, Veni Sancte Spiritus. Your line was come, father of the poor. Who had nothing to bring, and what did you bring them? Day six hundred seventy-one.

Christmas, Good Friday, Easter, Pentecost: each remembers something that happened, a birth, a death, a rising, a wind in a room. Trinity Sunday is different. Nothing happened on it. No event, no saint, no story. The week after Pentecost, having walked through the whole year of what God did, the Church stops and asks the question underneath all of it: who is God? A child raised Catholic is handed the answer before they have words for it, each time an adult traces a cross over them. Today, the feast of that answer.
screen: `A FEAST WITH NO EVENT.` → `WHO IS GOD?` → `AN ANSWER TRACED ON YOUR BODY.`

segments.voice: Here's a surprise first: the word Trinity isn't in the Bible. What's there is a pattern. At the end of Matthew, the risen Jesus sends the apostles out, in the Douay-Rheims: "baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost." Notice it says the name, singular, then three. Paul ends a letter to Corinth with the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Ghost. Early Christians found themselves praying to the Father, through the Son, in the Spirit, and needed words for what they were already doing. A writer in North Africa named Tertullian, arguing against a teacher called Praxeas, used the Latin trinitas, a threeness. Later, the councils of Nicaea and Constantinople gave the Creed Catholics still say on Sunday. The Church's teaching is one God in three persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit, each fully God, not three gods, and not one God wearing three masks. The Church calls it a mystery, which in its language doesn't mean a puzzle to give up on. It means something true that you can keep going deeper into forever. The feast itself spread slowly through the Middle Ages, until a pope put it on the calendar of the whole Church. There's a famous story that Saint Patrick explained the Trinity with a shamrock. It's lovely, and it's a later legend; his own writings don't mention it. What Catholics actually do every day is simpler. They touch forehead, chest and both shoulders, and say the name.
screen: `THE WORD ISN'T IN THE BIBLE.` · `TERTULLIAN: TRINITAS.` · `ONE GOD, THREE PERSONS.` · `A MYSTERY TO GO DEEPER INTO.` · then, large: `IN THE NAME OF THE FATHER, AND OF THE SON, AND OF THE HOLY GHOST.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: the sign of the cross, three times, slowly. Sit, and breathe. The first time, just do it, at your usual speed, and notice how quickly it's over. The second time, pause at each touch: forehead, chest, left shoulder, right shoulder. The third time, let each name take a whole breath. If you're not someone who makes the sign, simply sit and notice your breath going in, resting, going out. The bell holds the time.
Trinity Sunday. The Sunday after Pentecost, a feast of the mystery of one God in three persons. Today's word.
Your line: one god, three persons. Today, the next time you make the sign of the cross, or see someone make it, slow it down by one breath. Day six hundred seventy-one.

howItsDone: On the Sunday after Pentecost Catholics celebrate Trinity Sunday, wearing white at Mass and professing the Creed; every day Catholics mark themselves with the sign of the cross in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.

myth: the word Trinity appears in the Bible
the pattern is there, Father, Son and Spirit, but the word came later, in Tertullian's Latin.
in Catholic teaching, a mystery means a puzzle to give up on
it means something true you can keep going deeper into.
Matthew's baptism line says the name, singular, then three
in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.

fork.setup: a friend asks you to sum up the Church's teaching on God in one line. which matches the Creed?
options: three gods who work as a team.
one God who wears three masks.
one God in three persons, each fully God.
fork.reveal: one God in three persons. the early Church rejected both three gods and one God taking turns in three roles.

original.note: Latin: threeness, a trinity; used by Tertullian.

trapdoor: what you thought: a hard doctrine nobody understands.
what it means: one God in three persons, the answer Catholics trace on their bodies in the sign of the cross.
what a scholar hears: Tertullian's Latin trinitas, the councils of Nicaea and Constantinople, and the feast's slow spread through the Middle Ages.

sources.quoted: baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.

notes: Tertullian's use of trinitas c. 200–213 (Against Praxeas); Theophilus of Antioch used Greek trias earlier. Confirm 'around 200'.
Feast extended to the universal Church by John XXII in 1334; confirm.
Shamrock story: first attested centuries after Patrick, not in his Confessio; confirm.
Rejection of modalism (masks) and tritheism stated simply; confirm wording for a general audience.
